newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish court delays Stankevich extradition ruling.
newsitem.headline: Polish court delays Stankevich extradition ruling.

text.p: A Polish court on Wednesday adjourned a hearing on Russia's request to extradite a former adviser to President Boris Yeltsin, saying it needed evidence that he took a bribe, PAP news agency said.
Russian prosecutors accuse Sergei Stankevich, who was formerly also a deputy mayor of Moscow, of having accepted a $10,000 bribe in 1992 to allow a concert in Red Square.
Stankevich, detained by police in Warsaw last month on the strength of a warrant issued by Russia through Interpol, denies the charge and says he is a victim of political intrigue.
The Warsaw provincial court said Russia's application for extradition had not included any evidence that Stankevich had committed a crime and requested that this be provided.
It also asked Stankevich's lawyer to submit evidence to back his argument that the money cited by Russian prosecutors was a payment for lectures Stankevich gave in London.

Stankevich, who has said he will not oppose returning to Moscow to clear his name if he has assurances of a truly impartial hearing, said the Warsaw court ruling gave him greater confidence that his case would be dealt with justly.

He has announced he will apply for permanent residence status in Poland. He plans to write two books, including one on Stalin's 1940 Katyn massacre of Polish officers and officials, and hopes to work as a consultant.
Wednesday's edition of the Polish Gazeta Wyborcza newspaper published a letter from Moscow's former Mayor Gavriil Popov, arguing that Poland should not surrender Stankevich to Russia.
